clue.text: Prayer archdeacon at old university cuts in assembly, for example

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer set for a particular day in the Anglican liturgy

indicators.note: the archdeacon and university together slice into the word in, splitting it open

parts.note: taken as written
VEN, short for Venerable, is the title given to an archdeacon
OU, the Open University (or Oxford University)

explanation.surface: A clergyman's prayers at a former college interrupt a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' signals the archdeacon and university pieces splitting the word in. 'Assembly' is offered as one example of a group word, like a flock or herd, hence 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembly (of people) is a word naming a group as a single unit, which is the grammatical category meant.

clue.text: Repugnant church member's first attempt to win favour

indicators.note: the church member's letters are placed before the word for repugnant

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
repugnant means offensive

explanation.surface: A disgusting churchgoer makes a first try at winning people over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens with 'Repugnant', but 'first' tells you the church member part goes ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign of flattery and friendliness intended to gain support is the idiom described.

clue.text: One inclined to accommodate Republican student

indicators.note: the inclined one takes in the Republican, giving it room inside

parts.note: someone who leans or tilts is a leaner

explanation.surface: Someone sympathetic towards a Republican student, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One inclined' suggests a political leaning, but it is simply someone leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is someone learning, a pupil or trainee.

clue.text: See about painter turning up ahead of time

indicators.note: the see goes around the reversed painter, enclosing it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat (see) of a bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue, going upward means the painter's letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: Look at an artist arriving before the appointed hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese; ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving early means arriving before the expected or scheduled time.

clue.text: Objection raised over European woman's Mexican plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed objection sits above the rest
in a down clue lifting the word for objection flips its letters upward

parts.note: a but is an objection (no ifs or buts)
Rose is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A protest is made about a European lady's plant from Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: This fragrant white-flowered plant, Polianthes tuberosa, is native to Mexico.

clue.text: Fall guy showing energy around Court One

indicators.note: the energy word wraps round court and one

parts.note: vim means vigour or energy
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A scapegoat displays vigour in Court Number One.
explanation.walkthrough: Court One evokes Wimbledon's show court or a criminal court, but it is just CT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is someone made to take the blame, a dupe or scapegoat.

clue.text: Inescapable point absorbing City fairly regularly

indicators.note: the headland word takes in the City abbreviation

parts.note: a ness is a headland or point of land
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: every other letter of fairly is taken, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An unavoidable item soaks up the City quite consistently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is the City of London, whose postcode is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential or required cannot be avoided, so inescapable is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Marked by oneness, like posh people your article can upset

parts.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the three pieces are read upward

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Upper-class people who share one view may upset your piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but here reverses YR + A + TIN to NITARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unitary means forming a single whole, characterised by unity.

clue.text: One's not lost, presumably, behaving thus?

definitions.text: One's not lost, presumably, behaving thus?

parts.words: One's not lost, presumably, behaving thus
parts.note: the proverb says he who hesitates is lost, so someone not lost presumably acts without any pause

explanation.surface: Someone who has kept their way must be acting in a certain manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' is turned round: if you are not lost, you presumably did not hesitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without pause or doubt is the opposite of the proverb's fatal hesitation.

clue.text: Oddly I can bear oxygen, being not dependent on it

indicators.note: arranged oddly means the letters are set out in a strange order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Strangely I can tolerate oxygen, while not needing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition points back to oxygen in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaerobic organisms live and grow without requiring air or its life-giving gas.

clue.text: Marker Irish are able to put outside

indicators.note: the word for are able is placed around the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: can means are able

explanation.surface: The Irish can put up a marker outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones built as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: The 6 a French artist mostly has yen for?

definitions.note: 6-down's answer is necessary, so this reads the necessary, slang for cash

indicators.note: most of the painter's name is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: What does a French painter mostly long for?
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a longing in the surface but is the Japanese currency, Y. 'The 6' means 'the necessary', informal for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The necessary is a colloquial term for cash or funds needed.

clue.text: Restore charge for crossing a German thoroughfare

indicators.note: the charge spans and encloses the German article and street

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee
ein is German for a
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Bring back the toll for crossing a German road.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put back into a former position, to restore.

clue.text: Prediction favouring actors on Eastenders initially

indicators.note: in an across clue the actors come on, that is after, the E

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Eastenders is used

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors

explanation.surface: A prediction that supports the performers in EastEnders, the long-running BBC soap set in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction, especially of weather.

clue.text: Singer, bad lot, supporting one-time Nicaraguan guerrilla?

indicators.note: in a down clue the jumbled lot sits beneath and holds up the guerrilla

parts.note: the Contras were the rebels who fought Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s

indicators.note: bad means the letters of lot are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer, a rotten type, backs a former Nicaraguan rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is a female singer with the lowest voice range.

clue.text: Settle up with small state keeping first of primitive manuscripts

indicators.note: the two pieces hold the initial letter inside

parts.note: to settle up is to pay

indicators.note: only the opening letter of primitive is taken

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state

explanation.surface: Pay up, along with a tiny state that holds early primitive documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyri are ancient documents written on sheets of papyrus reed.

clue.text: Hard American con man briefly framing a German woman

indicators.note: the run of pieces surrounds the a, which sits after the first letter

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the con man word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a fraud is a swindler or impostor

explanation.surface: A tough American trickster quickly stitches up a German woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' has the whole run enclose the A, which lands second; it also plays on stitching someone up in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Hausfrau is the German word for a housewife.

clue.text: They all leave books on former alliance of nations

indicators.note: in an across clue the books come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: ex means former
EU, the European Union
NT, the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Everybody departs with volumes about a past union of countries.
explanation.walkthrough: This Latin stage direction, 'they go out', comes with a nod to Brexit: EX-EU.
explanation.definitionFit: This stage direction in plays tells several characters to go off together.

clue.text: Ban accordingly restricting business degree

indicators.note: the word for accordingly confines the degree inside it

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, accordingly
MBA, Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A prohibition that consequently limits a business qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade.

clue.text: Better territory ultimately — except for a S American rodent!

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: only the final letter of territory is used

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Better land in the end, except for one South American rodent!
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara of South America is the largest rodent in the world.

clue.text: A note spies left, avoiding contact with others

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A message from secret agents who departed, steering clear of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial describes someone shunning society and companionship.

clue.text: Follow lines about northern aristocrats

indicators.note: the word for follow goes round the northern abbreviation

parts.note: to get something is to follow or understand it
RY, railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Track the lines concerning northern nobles.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born upper classes just below the nobility.

clue.text: Gravity of appeal for help by son investing capital

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the capital goes inside

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
Berne is the capital of Switzerland

explanation.surface: The seriousness of a son's cry for help when investing capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money in the investing surface; it is the Swiss capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity in the sense of seriousness or solemnity of manner.

clue.text: Chairman once primarily reporting in antipodean language

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the late Chinese leader

indicators.note: the first letters of reporting and in

explanation.surface: A former Chinese leader chiefly reporting in a language from down under.
explanation.definitionFit: This Polynesian tongue is spoken by the indigenous people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Fellow touring the Italian financial centre

indicators.note: the man goes round, enclosing the Italian article

parts.note: a man is a fellow
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A man travels round the Italian business capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is Italy's chief commercial city and home of its stock exchange.

clue.text: Like pathological agents researchers originally stored in small bottle

indicators.note: the initial goes into the bottle as if kept there

parts.note: a vial is a small container for liquids

indicators.note: only the first letter of researchers is taken

explanation.surface: Disease germs kept by researchers in a little bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Viral relates to viruses, which are agents of disease.

clue.text: Exciting sixty minutes employed in working the land

indicators.note: the hour is put to work inside the farming word

parts.note: tilling is ploughing or cultivating soil
HR, an hour

explanation.surface: An hour spent ploughing the fields is a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling means causing excitement, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Loony role tunny plays? No way!

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A tuna fish given a mad part on stage? Certainly not!
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang: Nelly is from rhyming slang 'Nelly Duff' for puff, meaning life, so 'not on your life'.
explanation.definitionFit: This emphatic British refusal means certainly not, never.
